The kin selection theory suggests that an organisms altruistic behavior, such as warning others of a predator, is motivated by the desire to protect relatives who share its genes, increasing the chances of passing on its genetic material. This theory proposes that the risk to the individual is offset by the benefit to its kin, increasing the likelihood of survival and reproduction of its genes.
